- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75.00), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias correction in next 5–7 days.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk — add 2–5% downward buffer to forecast.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 75.00 for 3+ consecutive days, forecast should trend downward; if below 70.00, upward.
- Forecast horizon 30d is overly optimistic in high-event periods — reduce forecast slope by 10–15% when >15 events/30d.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.50), model often fails to capture volatility — increase forecast variance or add 1–2% stochastic adjustment.
- If recent auction supply events are frequent (e.g., 3+ per 30d), model underestimates downward pressure — adjust forecast downward by 1–3% per event.
